questions.prompt: Where the bishop had once dwelt, there now a deep silence lies.
questions.answer: Ubi episcopus ōlim habitāverat, ibi nunc altum silentium iacet.

questions.prompt: We do not know whither the fugitives fled through the dark woods.
questions.answer: Quō fugitīvī per silvās obscūrās fūgerint nescīmus.

questions.prompt: The scouts hastened to report whence so great a danger had arisen.
questions.answer: Explōrātōrēs, unde tantum discrīmen ortum esset, nūntiāre properāvērunt.

questions.prompt: Hither the weary soldiers came, whence they never returned.
questions.answer: Hūc mīlitēs fessī vēnērunt, unde numquam rediērunt.

questions.prompt: When the enemy attacked, then the citizens bravely took up arms.
questions.answer: Cum hostēs oppugnāvērunt, tum cīvēs fortiter arma cēpērunt.

questions.prompt: As often as the poet recited, so often the crowd eagerly applauded.
questions.answer: Quotiēns poēta recitābat, totiēns turba cupidē plausit.

questions.prompt: When will the parent return, whom we now so anxiously await?
questions.answer: Quandō pārēns redībit, quem nunc tam sollicitē exspectāmus?

questions.prompt: Then the fields were fertile; now they lie barren and abandoned.
questions.answer: Tunc agrī fēcundī erant; nunc sterilēs et dēsertī iacent.

questions.prompt: So fierce was the battle that few soldiers survived that day.
questions.answer: Tam ātrōx erat proelium ut paucī mīlitēs illum diem superessent.

questions.prompt: The wine, somewhat diluted, was divided among the guests.
questions.answer: Vīnum, aliquantum dīlūtum, inter convīvās dīvīsum est.

questions.prompt: The old man is now as greedy as once he was generous.
questions.answer: Tam avārus nunc est senex quam ōlim līberālis fuit.

questions.prompt: How greatly you fear death, of which you so rarely think!
questions.answer: Quam magnopere mortem timēs, dē quā tam rārō cōgitās!

questions.prompt: Somewhere in these mountains the exiles are hiding, though we scarcely believe it.
questions.answer: Alicubī in hīs montibus exsulēs latent, quamquam vix crēdimus.

questions.prompt: If ever the tyrant returns, the people will flee to some place afar.
questions.answer: Sī umquam tyrannus redierit, populus aliquō procul fugiet.

questions.prompt: From somewhere a rumor arose that the fleet had been destroyed.
questions.answer: Alicunde fāma orta est classem dēlētam esse.

questions.prompt: By this way the merchants used to travel, by that the shepherds drove their flocks.
questions.answer: Hāc mercātōrēs iter facere solēbant, illāc pāstōrēs gregēs agēbant.

questions.prompt: Where the road narrows, there the ambush was cleverly prepared.
questions.answer: Quā via angustātur, ibi īnsidiae callidē parātae sunt.

questions.prompt: Here the temple once stood; there, across the valley, the citadel rose.
questions.answer: Hīc templum ōlim stābat; illīc, trāns vallem, arx surgēbat.

questions.prompt: By some way or other the messenger slipped through the enemy's lines.
questions.answer: Aliquā nūntius per hostium ōrdinēs ēlāpsus est.

questions.prompt: Whither the raft would be carried by the current, no helmsman could foresee.
questions.answer: Quō ratis flūmine ferrētur, nūllus gubernātor praevidēre poterat.

questions.prompt: As often as the Danaans attacked, so often the walls of Troy repelled them.
questions.answer: Quotiēns Danaī oppugnāvērunt, totiēns Trōiae mūrī eōs reppulērunt.

questions.prompt: When the boy first entered the elementary school, then he began to fear the master.
questions.answer: Cum puer prīmum lūdum litterārium intrāvit, tum magistrum timēre coepit.

questions.prompt: Now he demands a bronze cauldron, which somewhere he had lost.
questions.answer: Nunc aēneum lebētem flāgitat, quem alicubī āmīserat.

questions.prompt: Where the river bends, there the fishermen have set their nets.
questions.answer: Ubi flūmen sē flectit, ibi piscātōrēs rētia sua posuērunt.

questions.prompt: By that way the legions marched, by which no army had ever passed before.
questions.answer: Eā viā legiōnēs contendērunt, quā nūllus exercitus umquam anteā trānsierat.

questions.prompt: Whence the plague had come, no physician could tell.
questions.answer: Unde pestis vēnisset, nūllus medicus dīcere poterat.

questions.prompt: Thither the pilgrims journeyed, where the sacred spring was said to gush.
questions.answer: Illūc peregrīnī iter fēcērunt, ubi fōns sacer scatēre dīcēbātur.

questions.prompt: As often as the trumpet sounded, so often the horsemen charged again.
questions.answer: Quotiēns tuba sonuit, totiēns equitēs iterum impetum fēcērunt.

questions.prompt: Now the harbor is calm, but then it raged with a savage storm.
questions.answer: Nunc portus tranquillus est, tum autem saevā tempestāte furēbat.

questions.prompt: When the messenger arrived, then the general summoned his officers.
questions.answer: Cum nūntius advēnit, tunc imperātor centuriōnēs suōs convocāvit.

questions.prompt: When will the fleet set sail, which we now await with such longing?
questions.answer: Quandō classis solvet, quam nunc tantō dēsīderiō exspectāmus?

questions.prompt: So great was the famine that the citizens somewhere sought roots to eat.
questions.answer: Tam gravis erat famēs ut cīvēs alicubī rādīcēs edendās quaererent.

questions.prompt: If ever you find the ring somewhere, restore it at once to its owner.
questions.answer: Sī umquam ānulum alicubī invēneris, statim dominō suō redde.

questions.prompt: The wine was somewhat sweeter than the merchant had promised.
questions.answer: Vīnum aliquantō dulcius erat quam mercātor prōmīserat.

questions.prompt: How bravely he once fought, who now trembles at every shadow!
questions.answer: Quam fortiter aliquandō pugnāvit, quī nunc ad omnem umbram tremit!

questions.prompt: If you do not yet see clearly, recollect.
questions.answer: Sī nōndum satis cernitis, recordāminī.

questions.prompt: But if I do not come when I can, he will be unfriendly.
questions.answer: Sīn cum potuerō nōn vēnerō, tum erit inimīcus.

questions.prompt: If he were at this time a private citizen, yet he ought to be appointed.
questions.answer: Sī prīvātus esset hōc tempore, tamen is erat dēligendus.

questions.prompt: I wish I had been he would not now be troubling us.
questions.answer: Utinam quidem fuissem! Molestus nōbīs nōn esset.

questions.prompt: They dreaded his cruelty as if he were present in person.
questions.answer: Crūdēlitātem horrērent velut sī cōram adesset.

questions.prompt: For even if you do not accomplish what you wish, still you will prove that death is not an evil.
questions.answer: Ut enim nōn efficiās quod vīs, tamen mors ut malum nōn sit efficiēs.

questions.prompt: Even if you had taken away nothing else, you ought to have been satisfied.
questions.answer: Etsī nihil aliud abstulissētis, tamen contentōs vōs esse oportēbat.

questions.prompt: Even if you have nothing to write, still write.
questions.answer: Etiam sī quod scrībās nōn habēbis, scrībitō tamen.

questions.prompt: Suppose you could have been mistaken, who does not see that you cannot have been deceived in this way?
questions.answer: Vērum ut errāre potuistī, sīc dēcipī tē nōn potuisse quis nōn videt?

questions.prompt: Though they are staggering under debt, they yet look forward to being lords and masters.
questions.answer: quamquam premuntur aere aliēnō, dominātiōnem tamen exspectant.

questions.prompt: Germanicus did not delay, though he was aware this was all made up.
questions.answer: haud cunctātus est Germānicus, quamquam fingī ea intellegeret.

questions.prompt: He grew pale perceptibly, though he is always a pale man.
questions.answer: expalluit notābiliter, quamvīs palleat semper.

questions.prompt: And even supposing everything turned out contrary to expectation, still they saw clearly that they had the advantage by sea.
questions.answer: ac iam ut omnia contrā opīniōnem acciderent, tamen sē plūrimum nāvibus posse perspiciēbant.

questions.prompt: Therefore, so a chance was given to fight hand to hand, they did not mind pitting one of their vessels against two of the enemy’s.
questions.answer: itaque dum locus comminus pugnandī darētur, aequō animō singulās bīnīs nāvibus obiciēbant.

questions.prompt: So you shall have time, so you will write something.
questions.answer: sīc scrībēs aliquid, sī vacābis.

questions.prompt: If Hejus had anything for sale, if he sold it at his own valuation, I stop enquiring why you bought.
questions.answer: sī quid vēnāle habuit Heius, sī id quantī aestimābat, tantī vēndidit, dēsinō quaerere cūr ēmeris.
